texts.preamble: Sawroop Kaanwar vs Ashoka S on 21 December, 2024 Scch-21 1 Mvc No.344/2024 Kabc0B0000792024 In The Court Of Xvii Addl. Judge, Court Of Small Causes & Member, M.A.C.T, Mayo Hall Unit, Bengaluru (Scch-21) Present : Vijaykumar S. Hiremath., B.Sc, L.Lb., Xvii Addl. Judge, Court of Small Causes & Member, M.A.C.T., Bengaluru. Dated this the 21st Day of December-2024 M.V.C. No.344/2024 Petitioner/s: 1. Sawroop Kaanwar
texts.facts: The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.7,50,000/- for the accidental injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident took place on 05.12.2023. 2. The Brief facts of the petitioner's case is as under: It is the case of the petitioner that on 05.12.2023 at about 03.30 p.m., petitioner was walking on the extreme side of the Belathur main road holding her mother hand and mother was walking carefully and cautiously by following all traffic rules and regulations and by observing on moving vehicle, at that time one motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-53-HQ-6528 ridden by its rider in a rash and negligent manner endangering to human life, came from opposite direction and dashed against the petitioner. Due to forced impact petitioner fell down and sustained grevious injuries. Immediately, petitioner was shifted to Aaxis Hospital, Bangalore, wherein first aid treatment was given and then shifted to Manipal Hospital, Bangalore, wherein she was treated as inpatient and petitioner has spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical, conveyance, nourishment, food, transport and other charges. The petitioner further submitted that, prior to the accident she was heal and healthy and aged about 07 years and was student. Due to injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner is not able to participate in any sports and lost his childhood happiness. Respondent No.1 is the owner of the offending vehicle and Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle. Hence, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner. Hence, the petitioner has filed this petition for a compensation of Rs.7,50,000/- with interest. 3. After service of notice, the respondents have appeared before the court through their counsels. Sawroop Kaanwar vs Ashoka S on 21 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104463617/ 2 The respondent No.1 appear through his counsel and filed written statement by denying the contents of the claim petition and also denying the rash and negligent riding of the offending vehicle. Further, this respondent submits that, the erred vehicle insured with the 2nd respondent, the insurance company and the policy is in force on the date of alleged accident and liability if any is subjected to the terms and conditions of the policy. The respondent No.2 appear through his counsel and filed written statement by denying the contents of the claim petition. Further, this respondent seeks protection u/s 147, 150, 134(c) and 158(6) of M. V. Act. Further this respondent submits that, the rider of offending was not holding valid and effective driving license to drive the vehicle as on the date of accident, hence this respondent is not obligated to indemnify the 2nd respondent. Further this respondent denies the rash and negligent riding by the rider of the offending vehicle and involvement of the said vehicle in the alleged accident. Further submitted that insured vehicle had no FC as on the date of alleged accident. Both the respondents denied the age, occupation and income of the petitioner. The petitioner colluding with the owner and police filed the false case. By these reasons, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.
texts.arguments: In a claim of compensation U/s.166 of M.V.Act 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Honble Apex Court in Kusum and others Vs. Satveer and others reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319. 16. As far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, I have relied on a decision reported in M.F.A. No.100090 of 2014 in between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others V/s The Divisional Manager, Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has awarded interest at the rate of 6%.
